text:
maya: heads-up: partner ingestion logs (s3://partner-telemetry/2026-03-21/) include several long base64 fields that match our Vault transit ciphertext pattern. flagged by alert rule `vault-wrap-detector` and escalated to sec channel. link: https://alerts.internal/xyz789
sec-bot: detection summary: matches=9 objects, score=0.92, rule=vault-wrap-detector, severity=high :warning:
olivia: copying output. can someone confirm these are actually wrapped ciphertexts and not just encoded blobs? I can run an offline decrypt attempt if we rotate keys first.
raj: do not attempt decrypt on unknown partner blobs. action plan I propose:
1) disable service account keys for ingest pipeline (temporary)
2) create new KMS key version and mark as pending for rewrap
3) update Vault transit config to point to new key version after rewrap
4) run rewrap sweep using `vault rewrap` endpoint in canary then global
5) run token and API key churn for any services that had access to affected SAs
6) preserve audit logs for forensic review (don't purge)

tomas: RBAC tweak idea: apply least-priv lift for 30m via short-lived grant instead of broad org changes. Add conditional allow on `iam.serviceAccounts.keys.create` only from deploy CI principal deny otherwise. Also push an org policy to block external principal SA key creation.
olivia: I'll prepare the canary script. plan to run on a single object and confirm new ciphertexts decrypt fine downstream. commands:
```
# canary revoke key
gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable KEY --iam-account=sa-partner@redwood-ops.iam.gserviceaccount.com || true
# run vault canary rewrap
curl -s -X POST "https://vault.internal/v1/transit/rewrap" -H "X-Vault-Token: $VAULT_TOKEN" -d '{"ciphertext":"OLD_CT"}'
```

olivia: also enabling extra log retention: `gcloud logging sinks update forensic-sink --add-filter="resource.type=build AND protoPayload.methodName: \"google.iam.admin.v1\""`

maya: tagging @oncall to hold any changes that create SA keys for 45m and to coordinate partner notification. please collect list of principals that accessed the affected bucket in the last 48h.
oncall: ack. will hold key creation and pause related deploys. starting collection: `gsutil ls -L gs://partner-telemetry/2026-03-21/` + access logs query.
raj: started KMS key version creation. one note: when creating new version set `protection_level` same as current to avoid incompat issues. after create I'll share KMS key id and start rewrap.
raj: update: new key version created: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/partner-keys/cryptoKeys/ingest-wrapping/cryptoKeyVersions/3. kicking off staged rewrap. do not modify vault wrapping config until I post `ok`.
sec-bot: audit reminder: tag all actions with incident id INC-2026-03121 and export logs to forensic bucket.
olivia: canary rewrap result: 3/3 objects rewrapped successfully. sample output:
```
[2026-03-21T21:14:02Z] rewrap ok: gs://partner-telemetry/2026-03-21/objA -> new_ct: c2FtcGxl...
```
olivia: running full sweep now with rate limit 200/min. will post progress.

maya: quick note on partner comms: draft skeleton in /docs/incidents/templates/partner-notify.md. I'll DM legal for wording. we'll need to include blast-radius, mitigations taken, and recommended rotation steps on their side.
tomas: after sweep, we should roll out an org-level constraint to prevent SA-key uploads from external CI unless triaged. I'll open a PR for the policy and link the audit findings.
raj: rewrap sweep finished: 9/9 success, avg latency 150ms. logs uploaded to gs://forensic-archive/INC-2026-03121/rewrap.log
raj: next: rotate any IAM keys that were created in the window. listing SAs with lastKeyCreatedAt within event window and queued rotation jobs.
oncall: monitoring deploy hold. will reopen deploys 1h after all rotations complete and sec review.
maya: creating incident ticket and assigning postmortem once we verify partner notif. assigning owners: raj (KMS + rewrap audit), olivia (rewrap scripts + logs), tomas (RBAC + org policy PR), maya (partner comms + incident writeup).
maya: thanks all. once partner confirms we'll close INC and move to post-incident audit. :white_check_mark:
